components.component:
(css) /* The count's line height is a number, not "normal": with "normal" a line
   takes the tallest face drawn in it, and Arabic-Indic digits are drawn in
   Noto Sans Arabic, whose ascent and descent are much larger than Plex
   Mono's, so the chip grew when that font arrived. A number sizes the line
   from the first face of the stack alone, whatever face draws the digits.
   The same holds for StatBar's values and RecordList's meta. */
.stoa-filter-chip__count

components.component:
(css) /* Every line takes a set height instead of the face's own ascent and
   descent (line-height: normal), so a line drawn in a fallback face before
   the web fonts arrive is as tall as it is after them, and nothing on the
   page moves when they do: an AppHeader's title, a panel's title, a
   field's label. Set on the root and inherited; :where keeps it at zero
   specificity, so an application's own line height wins, and a component
   that sets one keeps it. Text that wraps as prose keeps this one. One-line
   chrome sets the tight line height in its own rule: buttons and the
   controls built on them, tabs, a disclosure's summary, field labels, titles and headings in bars and panels (but not AppHeader's title, see
   there), badges and deadlines, counts in bars, chart and calendar labels.
   A tight line is still a set height, so it keeps its height when the
   fonts arrive as well. */
:where(:root)

(css) /* The count's line height is a number, not "normal": with "normal" a line
   takes the tallest face drawn in it, and Arabic-Indic digits are drawn in
   Noto Sans Arabic, whose ascent and descent are much larger than Plex
   Mono's, so the chip grew when that font arrived. A number sizes the line
   from the first face of the stack alone, whatever face draws the digits.

.stoa-filter-chip__count
